questions.question: The ________ invaders were followed by the Sakas and Huns.
questions.explanation: Greek invaders were followed by the Sakas and Huns.

questions.question: Who is the writer of 'Little Girls Wiser Than Men'?
questions.explanation: 'Little Girls Wiser Than Men' is a short story by Leo Tolstoy.

questions.question: Akoulya started to make a channel with the help of a ________.
questions.explanation: In Leo Tolstoy's 'Little Girls Wiser Than Men', Akoulya dug a channel with a stick/rod.

questions.question: All the invaders appeared on the scene as ________ but were absorbed in the ranks of the vanquished.
questions.explanation: Invaders arrived as victors yet were absorbed into the culture/ranks of the vanquished.

questions.question: The young people were unable to hold their ________.
questions.explanation: The young people could not hold back their tears.

questions.question: Aris says that genuine ________ and peace is more precious than diamond or silver or gold.
questions.explanation: In 'The Acceptance Speech', Alexander Aris emphasizes genuine brotherhood and peace.

questions.question: The parents did not ________ the feelings of Sun and Moon.
questions.explanation: In 'Sun and Moon', the parents failed to understand the children's feelings.

questions.question: The author ordered ________ pairs of shoes, though he wanted only two.
questions.explanation: In 'Quality', the narrator felt compelled to order more pairs than he actually needed.

questions.question: In the fifth year of imprisonment, the lawyer asked for ________.
questions.explanation: In Anton Chekhov's 'The Bet', during the fifth year the prisoner asked for wine and played music.

questions.question: Munni advised Halku to pay the landlord after the ________ season was over.
questions.explanation: In 'January Night' ('Poos Ki Raat'), Munni suggested paying after the harvesting season.

questions.question: Immunoglobulin is a protein acting as an ________.
questions.explanation: Immunoglobulins are proteins that function as antibodies.

questions.question: There are ________ general approaches to the treatment of allergy diseases.
questions.explanation: There are three general approaches to treating allergic diseases.

questions.question: When Gillu was happy, he made a sound of ________.
questions.explanation: In 'Gillu', the squirrel made a soft 'chik-chik' sound when happy.

questions.question: People nowadays think ________ than ancient times.
questions.explanation: In 'The Pace for Living', modern life makes people think faster.

questions.question: The poet says that life is ________ because it is full of troubles.
questions.explanation: Surrounded by troubles and sorrows, life feels bitter.

questions.question: Who composed 'Ode on Solitude'?
questions.explanation: 'Ode on Solitude' was written by Alexander Pope.

questions.question: 'Hurt' is such a ________ polythene bag.
questions.explanation: In 'Polythene Bag', hurt is compared to a strange polythene bag.

questions.question: Vidyapati's poems are about Radha and ________.
questions.explanation: Vidyapati's devotional lyrics centre on Radha and Krishna.

questions.question: Mr. Gessler was a ________ shoemaker settled in London.
questions.explanation: In 'Quality', Mr. Gessler was a German-born master shoemaker in London.

questions.question: The chairs for the party came in the ________.
questions.explanation: In 'Sun and Moon', the party chairs arrived in the afternoon.

questions.question: In 'Two Horizons', letters were exchanged between ________.
questions.explanation: 'Two Horizons' consists of letters between a mother and her daughter.

questions.question: The narrator lived with his girlfriend for ________ years.
questions.explanation: In 'Love Defiled', the narrator lived with his girlfriend for eight years.

questions.question: The mother tells her daughter that her ________ will disappear slowly on its own.
questions.explanation: In 'Two Horizons', the mother reassures her daughter that her discontent will gradually fade.

questions.question: The narrator's girlfriend was wearing a dress of his favourite colour ________ during their last meeting before separation.
questions.explanation: She wore a yellow dress during their final meeting.

questions.question: The poet calls things like health and virtue ________.
questions.explanation: Health and virtue are regarded as precious gifts of life.

questions.question: Vidyapati is a ________ poet.
questions.explanation: Vidyapati (Mahakavi Vidyapati) is a renowned Maithili and Sanskrit poet.

questions.question: The happy man is content to get his food from his ________.
questions.explanation: In 'Ode on Solitude', the contented man gets food from his own fields.

questions.question: "The Empty Heart" highlights man's insatiable ________.
questions.explanation: 'The Empty Heart' critiques insatiable greed.

questions.question: Munni was Halku's ________.
questions.explanation: In Premchand's 'January Night', Munni is Halku's wife.

questions.question: The banker had given a party ________ years ago.
questions.explanation: In 'The Bet', the banker had hosted the party fifteen years earlier.

questions.question: Hope for the Indian cinema lies in the simplification of ________ and content.
questions.explanation: Satyajit Ray emphasizes simplifying style and content in Indian cinema.

questions.question: Gillu refused to eat ________ when the author was in the hospital.
questions.explanation: In 'Gillu', the squirrel refused his favourite kaju (cashew) while the narrator was hospitalized.

questions.question: Burning the leaves is not good for the ________.
questions.explanation: Burning dry leaves pollutes the air and harms the ecology.

questions.question: It is hard to get people to work for ________.
questions.explanation: In 'Me and the Ecology Bit', the narrator finds it hard to get people to act for ecology.

questions.question: Slow thinkers are handicapped in the business of getting ________.
questions.explanation: In 'The Pace for Living', slow thinkers are at a disadvantage in earning a living in modern fast-paced society.

questions.question: An Indian film should steer clear of ________.
questions.explanation: Satyajit Ray notes films should avoid inconsistencies.

questions.question: Sun and Moon are the names of ________.
questions.explanation: In Katherine Mansfield's 'Sun and Moon', Sun and Moon are the children.

questions.question: The daughter in 'Two Horizons' does not wish to ________ any more.
questions.explanation: In 'Two Horizons', the daughter says she no longer wishes to dream.

questions.question: The narrator's girlfriend in 'Love Defiled' was very ________.
questions.explanation: The narrator describes his girlfriend as intelligent.

questions.question: Gillu had stopped ________ the day he died.
questions.explanation: In 'Gillu', the squirrel stopped eating on the day he passed away.

questions.question: 'The Acceptance Speech' was delivered by Alexander Aris in ________.
questions.explanation: The Nobel Peace Prize ceremony/acceptance speech took place in Oslo.

questions.question: No Indian cinema can be ________ on all counts.
questions.explanation: Satyajit Ray states no Indian cinema can be demeaned on all counts.

questions.question: In the poem 'The Sleeping Porter', the ________ are snow-clad.
questions.explanation: In 'The Sleeping Porter', snow-clad peaks rise above the exhausting climb.

questions.question: The Koel is restless for her ________.
questions.explanation: In Puran Singh's 'The Koel', the bird pines restlessly for her beloved.

questions.question: To gather gold, the rich man tried all ________.
questions.explanation: In 'The Empty Heart', he explored all avenues to amass gold.

questions.question: Radha is hurt and ________.
questions.explanation: In 'Radha', she is hurt and sad.

questions.question: The polythene bag cannot be ________.
questions.explanation: In 'Polythene Bag', it cannot be easily destroyed.

questions.question: A happy man spends his leisure in ________.
questions.explanation: In 'Ode on Solitude', leisure is spent in peaceful recreation.

questions.question: Jim has a ________ route.
questions.explanation: In 'Me and the Ecology Bit', Jim has a paper route.

questions.question: The author tried to feed Gillu some ________.
questions.explanation: In 'Gillu', the author tried feeding him fruit juice.

questions.question: How many blocks away was the post office from Mr. Johnson's house?
questions.explanation: In 'Me and the Ecology Bit', the post office was two blocks away.

questions.question: One of the most significant phenomena of our time has been the development of ________.
questions.explanation: Satyajit Ray highlights the rise of cinema as a major phenomenon of our time.

questions.question: Who delivered the speech while accepting the Nobel Peace Prize on behalf of Aung San Suu Kyi?
questions.explanation: Her son Alexander Aris delivered the speech in Oslo.

questions.question: The old woman in the piece 'Once Upon a Time' is a daughter of ________.
questions.explanation: In Toni Morrison's 'Once Upon a Time', the old woman is a daughter of slaves.

questions.question: The man was rich, but not ________.
questions.explanation: In 'The Empty Heart', despite his wealth, the man was not content.

questions.question: Who wrote the poem 'Koel'?
questions.explanation: 'The Koel' ('Koel') was written by Puran Singh.

questions.question: The poet asks the Koel what keeps it ________, yet charred.
questions.explanation: The poet asks what keeps the koel fresh despite its dark/charred plumage.

questions.question: The porter carries a load of 25 kilos on his ________.
questions.explanation: In 'The Sleeping Porter', the porter carries a heavy load on his back.

questions.question: Martha's eyes were as tranquil as ________.
questions.explanation: In Walter de la Mare's 'Martha', her eyes were as tranquil as silence.

questions.question: The ________ of the children stood still in the hush of age gone by.
questions.explanation: In 'Martha', the hearts of the children stood still as she narrated.

questions.question: Direct speech of: I asked her why she was sad is:
options: I told her, "Why you sad are?"
I said to her, "Why sad you are?"
I said to her, "Why are you sad?"
I telling her, "Why you sad are?"
questions.explanation: 'Why she was sad' converts back to direct question '"Why are you sad?"'

questions.question: Direct speech of: Ramesh asked me where I was going is:
options: Ramesh said to her, "Where is she going?"
Ramesh said to me, "Where are you going?"
Ramesh will say, "Where do you go?"
questions.explanation: 'Asked me where I was going' converts back to 'Ramesh said to me, "Where are you going?"'

questions.question: Direct speech of: She wished that I might be happy is:
options: She said to me, "May you be happy!"
She will say, "Happy you may be."
She may say, "You may be happy."
questions.explanation: Optative wish 'wished that I might be happy' corresponds to 'She said to me, "May you be happy!"'

questions.question: Indirect speech of: Rohan said to me, "Please give me a book." is:
options: Rohan requests me to give a book him.
Rohan asked me to give a book to him.
Rohan requested me to give him a book.
Rohan may request me for a book.
questions.explanation: 'Please' indicates a polite request: 'Rohan requested me to give him a book.'

questions.question: Indirect speech of: He said, "Alas! I am ruined." is:
options: He said with sorrow that he is ruined.
He will say that he was ruined.
He says that he can be ruined.
He exclaimed with sorrow that he was ruined.
questions.explanation: 'Alas!' becomes 'exclaimed with sorrow' and 'am ruined' shifts to 'was ruined'.

questions.question: Indirect speech of: He said to the boy: Do not play in the sun is:
options: He forbade the boy to play in the sun.
He requested the boy to not play in the sun.
He says to the boy to not play in the sun.
He ordered the boy not to play in the sun.
questions.explanation: 'He ordered the boy not to play in the sun.' is the grammatically complete indirect command.

questions.question: Always beware ________ dubious people.
questions.explanation: 'Beware of' is the standard preposition used with 'beware'.

questions.question: Do not hanker ________ wealth.
questions.explanation: 'Hanker after' is the standard idiom meaning to strongly crave or pursue.

questions.question: He deals ________ his friends decently.
questions.explanation: 'Deal with' means to behave or interact with someone.

questions.question: We should abstain ________ drinking.
questions.explanation: 'Abstain from' is the standard preposition used with abstaining from a habit.

questions.question: It has been raining ________ Monday.
questions.explanation: 'Since' is used before a specific point in time like 'Monday'.

questions.question: We should not laugh ________ the poor.
questions.explanation: 'Laugh at' is the standard preposition when mocking or ridiculing.

questions.question: What is wrong ________ you?
questions.explanation: 'Wrong with' is standard in 'What is wrong with you?'

questions.question: You ________ do it.
questions.explanation: 'Should' is followed directly by the base verb 'do'.

questions.question: ________ has ruined him.
questions.explanation: Gerund 'Drinking' acts as the subject of the sentence.

questions.question: He has ________ hard.
questions.explanation: 'Has to work' expresses obligation/necessity.

questions.question: I will learn ________.
questions.explanation: 'Learn + gerund' ('riding') is natural and grammatically acceptable here.

questions.question: ________ my anger.
questions.explanation: 'Controlled' works as the past participle/verb form in the given options.

questions.question: ________ is a good exercise.
questions.explanation: Gerund 'Walking' serves as the subject before 'is a good exercise'.

questions.question: He would like to ________ you.
questions.explanation: After 'to', the base form of the verb 'see' is used.

questions.question: Synonym of 'Virtue' is:
questions.explanation: 'Goodness' is a synonym of 'virtue'.

questions.question: Synonym of 'Blame' is:
questions.explanation: 'Accuse' means to charge or blame someone.

questions.question: Antonym of 'Bold' is:
questions.explanation: 'Timid' (shy/fearful) is the opposite of 'bold'.

questions.question: Antonym of 'Foe' is:
questions.explanation: 'Friend' is the antonym of 'foe' (enemy).

questions.question: Active voice of: By whom has the snake been killed? is:
questions.explanation: Present perfect passive 'By whom has ... been killed?' converts to 'Who has killed the snake?'

questions.question: Active voice of: The prize can be won by him. is:
options: He has to win the prize.
He may try to win the prize.
questions.explanation: 'Can be won by him' converts to active 'He can win the prize.'

questions.question: Active voice of: Is a story being written by him? is:
options: Will he be able to write a story?
questions.explanation: Present continuous passive 'Is a story being written by him?' converts to 'Is he writing a story?'

questions.question: Passive voice of: He helped the old man. is:
options: The old man is helping by him.
The man is too old to be helped.
The old man was helped by him.
The old man has been helped by him.
questions.explanation: Simple past active 'helped' becomes simple past passive 'was helped by him'.

questions.question: Active voice of: Let the poor be not insulted. is:
questions.explanation: Negative imperative passive 'Let the poor be not insulted.' converts to 'Do not insult the poor.'

questions.question: Passive voice of: My brother is to plant the tree. is:
options: The tree is planted by my brother.
The tree is to be planted by my brother.
Planted is the tree by my brother.
By my brother is the tree planted.
questions.explanation: 'Is to + V1' converts to passive 'is to be + V3' ('The tree is to be planted by my brother.').

questions.question: Translate into English: रोज अखबार पढ़ो।
questions.explanation: 'Read the newspaper daily.' is the natural imperative sentence.

questions.question: Translate into English: जो वह कहता है, सही है।
questions.explanation: 'What he says is right.' accurately translates the sentence.

questions.question: Translate into English: गलती करना मनुष्य का स्वभाव है।
questions.explanation: 'To err is human.' is the well-known proverb/translation.
